intro.lead: From User Insight to Pixel-Perfect Prototypes
intro.desc: I turn research, flows, and information architecture into accessible, responsive experiences for web and mobile.
intro.hand: Pick a skill to see it in motion

items.title: User Research
items.label: User Research
items.desc: Learning who a product is for and what they are trying to get done, before deciding what to design.

items.title: User Flows
items.label: User Flows
items.desc: Mapping the steps someone takes to reach a goal, so gaps and detours show up early.

items.title: User Personas
items.label: User Personas
items.desc: Turning research into a clear picture of the people I am designing for.

items.title: Information Architecture
items.label: Info Architecture
items.desc: Organising content and navigation so people find things where they expect them.

items.title: Wireframing
items.label: Wireframing
items.desc: Sketching structure and layout early, before colour and polish get in the way.

items.title: Prototyping
items.label: Prototyping
items.desc: Making ideas clickable so flows can be tried and discussed before anything is built.

items.title: Web & Mobile App Design
items.label: Web & mobile
items.desc: Designing interfaces for browsers and phones with each platform's habits in mind.

items.title: Responsive Design
items.label: Responsive
items.desc: Making layouts adapt gracefully from a small phone to a wide desktop.

items.title: Visual Hierarchy
items.label: Hierarchy
items.desc: Using size, weight, spacing and contrast so the eye lands on what matters first.

items.title: Design Principles
items.label: Principles
items.desc: Balance, consistency, proximity and contrast: the basics behind choices I can explain.

items.title: Accessibility (WCAG basics)
items.label: Accessibility
items.desc: Colour contrast, readable text, touch targets and keyboard-friendly patterns, so more people can use a product.

items.title: AI-Assisted Ideation
items.label: AI ideation
items.desc: Using AI tools to explore directions and questions faster, then judging the results myself.
